correctness.rationale: On a complete multipartite graph, equality-or-nonadjacency is exactly an equivalence relation whose classes are the parts, and adjacency is quantifier-free recoverable. For all nontrivial targets the candidate defining rank is at least three, so a rank-three transitivity sentence for equality-or-nonadjacency excludes arbitrary non-multipartite competitors without increasing the rank; the one-vertex case is immediate. The rank-\(q\) Ehrenfeucht-Fraïssé profile for one finite equivalence relation is correctly encoded by the truncated cumulative counts \(N_k\) and exact counts \(C_k\). Rewriting same-profile competitors in cumulative-count differences gives precisely the stated pinned, tight one-sided, exact-edge, and slack constraints. Zero upper and lower bounds propagate in the two directed paths, and failure of either propagation leaves a one-unit feasible perturbation; successful propagation forces every difference to zero. The frozen checker was inspected and tests both the EF-profile equivalence and path criterion on bounded exhaustive families; an additional independent symbolic/small-case reconstruction in this run agreed with the profile mechanism. Finite checks are only corroborative.
correctness.risk: The central infinite step is the rank-profile characterization for a single finite equivalence relation; the proof supplies a Duplicator invariant rather than relying on the finite checker.

value.rationale: Logical depth is a standard descriptive-complexity invariant and complete multipartite graphs form a canonical symmetry-rich class. The theorem gives a complete exact classification for every heterogeneous part-size multiset, recovers important subfamilies, and turns the answer into a linear-time two-pass criterion. That is a natural structural result, not an arbitrary finite computation.
value.risk: The result is elementary enough that its main residual value risk is hidden folklore priority, which is recorded under originality.

final_claim: For every finite nonempty complete multipartite graph, ordinary first-order logical depth is exactly the least \(q\) satisfying the submitted two directed reachability tests built from the distinct part sizes and multiplicities; the test is linear in the number of distinct sizes and yields the stated uniform-part and biclique corollaries.
limitations: Ordinary first-order logic without counting quantifiers only.
